title: Who installs the SSL inspection certificate on Client Connector devices, per platform
aliases: when does zcc install the certificate

prose.text: Inspected traffic is re-signed with a Zscaler certificate, so the device must trust the Zscaler root: [[zia.ssl-inspection.certificates:root-must-be-trusted]]. {{who-installs}}

rows: {{ios}} {{ios-intune-profile}} Which MDM payload the vendor recommends for other MDMs is open {{gap:ios-payload}}.
Only user traffic can be inspected: [[zia.ssl-inspection.certificates:chromeos]]. {{chromeos-flex}}

prose.text: On mobile devices the certificate goes through MDM in any case: [[zia.ssl-inspection.certificates:mobile-mdm]]. Named deployment channels beyond the macOS profiles above remain open in [[zia.ssl-inspection.certificates]].

prose.label: In the app profile and the API.
prose.text: The setting, and the custom certificate that can replace Zscaler's, belong to the app profile: [[zcc.app-profiles.ssl-certificate:install-option]]; the iOS profile has no such setting: [[zcc.app-profiles.ssl-certificate:no-ios-option]]. The Go SDK sends the macOS key in snake_case, and its model says the camelCase form was silently ignored: [[zcc.api.web-policy-wire:mac-snake-or-ignored]].

checks.do: Whether Install Zscaler SSL Certificate is enabled in the app profile for the device's platform (Windows, Linux, macOS before Big Sur).
On macOS 11 or later, iOS and Android, whether the MDM pushes the root certificate.
After uploading a new certificate, whether the device has since enrolled, checked in for a modified profile, updated, or had Update Policy clicked.

who-installs.statement: Depending on the platform, either Client Connector or the MDM installs the Zscaler SSL certificate that SSL inspection needs.

quotes: Depending on the platform, Zscaler Client Connector or your Mobile Device Management (MDM) solution installs the Zscaler SSL certificate required for SSL inspection.

desktop-toggle.statement: For Windows, Linux and macOS, Client Connector installs the certificate automatically when Install Zscaler SSL Certificate is enabled in the platform's app profile (on macOS only before Big Sur 11; see big-sur).
desktop-toggle.conditions: The macOS limit was appended after verification so the claim does not mislead when read alone.

quotes: In the Zscaler Admin Console, enable Zscaler Client Connector to automatically install the Zscaler SSL certificate on your users’ devices for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
On the App Profiles tab, click Add <OS Version> Policy or select an existing policy to edit.
Enable Install Zscaler SSL Certificate.
Install Zscaler SSL Certificate is not supported on devices running macOS Big Sur (11) and later.

big-sur.statement: Install Zscaler SSL Certificate is not supported on devices running macOS Big Sur (11) and later.

quotes: Install Zscaler SSL Certificate is not supported on devices running macOS Big Sur (11) and later.

macos-mdm-profile.statement: The macOS deployment guides push the CA certificate needed for SSL inspection with a certificate configuration profile from the MDM (a Certificate payload in Jamf Pro with Allow all apps access, a Trusted certificate template in Intune), using the Zscaler root certificate downloaded from Internet Access > Resources > SSL Intermediate Certificate, or a custom root or intermediate.

quotes: If you use Internet & SaaS and you want to perform SSL inspection, you must configure a certificate profile to push the Certificate Authority (CA) certificate required for SSL inspection.
You can use the default Zscaler CA certificate or a custom Root or Intermediate CA certificate.
Enable the Allow all apps access option and Save the profile.
From the navigation menu, go to Internet Access > Resources > SSL Intermediate Certificate.
In the View Zscaler Intermediate CA Certificate window, under the Root Certificate field, click Download.
Template name: Choose Trusted certificate.

android.statement: On Android, Client Connector does not install the certificate automatically and Zscaler recommends installing the root through the MDM; it installs certificates only on Samsung devices with administrator privileges, from Install Certificates in the app's More window.

quotes: For Android, Zscaler Client Connector does not automatically install the certificate. Zscaler recommends installing the root certificate using your MDM.
Zscaler Client Connector only installs certificates for Samsung devices that have administrator privileges.
To install the certificate, go to the More window in Zscaler Client Connector and click Install Certificates.

android-7.statement: From Android 7.0, non-default certificate authorities are not trusted by apps unless the app's developer explicitly allows it, so the Zscaler certificate is not trusted by such apps.

quotes: For Android version 7.0 and later, Google prevents non-default certificate authorities from being trusted.
Unless the third-party application developer explicitly allows it, the Zscaler certificate or any third-party certificate is not trusted.

ios.statement: On iOS, Client Connector does not automatically install the certificate, because Apple requires certificates installed by an application to be untrusted by default; Zscaler recommends installing the root through the MDM.

quotes: For iOS, Zscaler Client Connector does not automatically install the certificate because Apple requires application-installed certificates to be untrusted by default. Zscaler recommends installing the root certificate using your MDM.

ios-intune-profile.statement: For iOS, the Intune guide pushes the CA certificate for SSL inspection with a certificate profile for the iOS/iPadOS platform using the Trusted Certificate template and the uploaded .crt file; the certificate is the default Zscaler Central Authority certificate (found under Internet Access > Resources > SSL Intermediate Certificate, in the ZscalerRootCerts.zip file to unzip) or a custom Root CA certificate.

quotes: If you use Internet & SaaS and you want to perform SSL inspection, you must configure a certificate profile to push the Certificate Authority certificate required for SSL inspection.
You can use the default Zscaler Central Authority (CA) certificate or a custom Root CA certificate.
From the navigation menu, go to Internet Access > Resources > SSL Intermediate Certificate.
Template name: Select Trusted Certificate.
On the Configuration Settings tab, upload the .crt file to Intune and click Next.
Navigate to the ZscalerRootCerts.zip file and unzip it.

evidence.after: Step 3: (Optional) Configure a Certificate Configuration Profile
quotes: Platform: Select iOS/iPadOS.

workspace-one-macos.statement: In the Workspace ONE UEM macOS guide, the unzipped root certificate file is renamed to a .crt extension, uploaded and attached in the profile, and Allow access to all applications is enabled.

quotes: Navigate to the ZscalerRootCerts.zip file, unzip it, and rename the file extension to .crt.
Select Choose File, upload the ZscalerRootCerts.crt file, and click Attach Certificate.
Enable the Allow access to all applications setting.

chromeos-flex.statement: The ChromeOS Flex guide says the certificates must be installed manually on ChromeOS Flex, Android and iOS devices, or using the Google Admin console; for ChromeOS Flex, the certificate is uploaded in the Google Admin console under Devices > Networks for an organizational unit, in the Certificates section, selecting the platform for which the certificate acts as a certificate authority.

quotes: The certificates must be installed manually on ChromeOS Flex, Android, and iOS devices, or using the Google Admin console.
For ChromeOS Flex, the certificate can be installed on the Google Admin console.
Go to Devices > Networks.
Under Organization units, select the organizational unit where you want to apply the certificate.
In the Certificates section, click Upload Certificate.
Select the platform (e.g., ChromeOS Flex) for which this certificate acts as a certificate authority.

install-events.statement: The certificate is imported on enrollment, when the admin modifies the app profile and the device checks in for it, when Client Connector updates, and when the user clicks Update Policy; each time, Client Connector gets the certificate link from the Admin Console and attempts the installation.

quotes: The Internet & SaaS service imports the certificate in the following situations:
Upon enrollment
If the admin modifies the app profile and the device checks in to download the new profile
When Zscaler Client Connector updates
When the user clicks Update Policy for Zscaler Client Connector
When these events occur, Zscaler Client Connector receives the certificate link from the Zscaler Admin Console and attempts to install the certificate.

replacement.statement: When a certificate is already deployed and a new one is uploaded, Client Connector installs it with a native Windows method, replacing the existing certificate if it is new or different and leaving it alone if it is the same.

quotes: If a certificate is already deployed and you upload a new certificate, Zscaler Client Connector uses a native Windows method to install the certificate.
The app automatically replaces the certificate if it’s new or different, but won’t change it if the same certificate already exists.

ios-payload.title: Which MDM payload installs the root on iOS
ios-payload.detail: The SSL inspection article recommends the MDM for iOS but names no payload type or certificate identifier. The Intune iOS guide describes a certificate profile (ios-intune-profile); no source read here gives the payload for other MDMs on iOS.
